overview: Transform one-time customers into lifetime advocates and referral sources. Master the post-installation relationship building that generates yard signs, 5-star reviews, and consistent referrals. This module teaches you how to create a self-sustaining pipeline of new business through exceptional customer service and strategic follow-up systems.
learningObjectives: Build lasting relationships beyond the installation
Generate referrals through strategic post-install follow-up
Secure yard sign placements for neighborhood marketing
Create customer advocates who promote Roof-ER proactively
Maintain contact with customers for long-term referral generation
Turn satisfied customers into your best marketing channel

successStories.title: Lisa's Referral Machine: 47 Sign-Ups from One Street
successStories.metric: 47 referral sign-ups in 6 months from one initial customer
successStories.story:
Lisa signed up the Martinez family on Oakwood Drive in April. Great installation, happy customer. But Lisa did not stop there.

Week 1 post-install: Called Mrs. Martinez personally. Asked for yard sign placement. Mrs. Martinez agreed. Sent review link via text. Mrs. Martinez posted glowing 5-star review.

Week 2: Lisa asked for referrals. Mrs. Martinez mentioned three neighbors who commented on the work. Lisa knocked those three houses the same day. Two had damage. Both signed up.

Month 2: Lisa called Mrs. Martinez again during storm season. 'Anyone else on your street mention needing inspection?' Mrs. Martinez gave four more names. Lisa converted three.

Month 3-6: Lisa checked in quarterly. Each time, Mrs. Martinez thought of 2-3 more neighbors. The yard sign generated inbound calls. The review was shown to prospects during door knocking.

Total result: ONE satisfied customer generated 47 sign-ups over six months. Lisa's commission from that single relationship: over 95,000 dollars.

The secret? Lisa treated Mrs. Martinez like a long-term partner, not a one-time transaction. She checked in regularly, made referrals easy, and always followed through.
successStories.keyTakeaway: One exceptional customer relationship can generate years of referrals if you stay in touch and make it easy for them to help you.

successStories.title: Brandon's Service Recovery Win: From Complaint to Biggest Advocate
successStories.metric: Turned angry customer into 12 direct referrals
successStories.story:
The Johnsons were furious. Installation finished, but production crew left nails in the driveway. Mrs. Johnson called Brandon livid. 'This is unacceptable. I am posting a bad review.'

Brandon's response was immediate and decisive:

Step 1 - Acknowledge: 'Mrs. Johnson, you are absolutely right. That should never have happened. I am so sorry.'

Step 2 - Ownership: 'I am personally coming over today to make this right.'

Step 3 - Action: Brandon arrived 2 hours later with magnetic roller, spent 90 minutes sweeping every inch of driveway and yard. Found 47 nails. Showed Mrs. Johnson the full bucket. 'All gone.'

Step 4 - Beyond: Brandon also noticed gutter slightly misaligned. Called production supervisor. Fixed same day. Did not ask, just handled it.

Step 5 - Follow-up: Called Mrs. Johnson next day. 'I want to make sure you are completely satisfied now. Is there anything else we can do?'

Mrs. Johnson's response: 'Brandon, I have never had a contractor care this much. You turned a nightmare into the best experience.'

Result: Mrs. Johnson posted 5-star review specifically praising Brandon's service recovery. She told the story at her book club, church group, and to neighbors. Twelve direct referrals in four months.

Brandon's lesson: 'Customers with problems you fix become stronger advocates than customers who never had problems. Service recovery is your moment to shine.'
successStories.keyTakeaway: Problems fixed exceptionally well create more powerful advocates than perfect experiences. Service recovery is a sales opportunity.

successStories.title: Nicole's Long Game: 3-Year Customer Turns Into 31 Referrals
successStories.metric: 31 sign-ups from one customer relationship over 3 years
successStories.story:
Nicole helped the Patels get a new roof in year one. Good experience, nice family. Nicole did the basics - yard sign, review request, initial referral ask. Got 2 referrals in month one.

But Nicole did something most reps do not do: She stayed in touch.

Year 1, Quarterly: Called Mr. Patel every 3 months. 'Storm season is here, anyone you know need inspection?' Generated 3 more referrals.

Year 2, Semi-Annual: Reduced to twice yearly. Spring and fall. Each call: 'How's the roof holding up? Anyone in your circle mention storm damage?' Generated 8 more referrals.

Year 3, Annual: Called once in spring. 'Mr. Patel, it has been three years since we did your roof. Hope it is still looking great! Storm came through last week - anyone you know affected?' Generated 18 referrals.

Why the increase? Mr. Patel's friends were now experiencing their own storm damage. Timing + trust + top-of-mind = referrals.

Nicole's system:
- Set quarterly reminders in phone for first year
- Semi-annual for year two
- Annual forever after
- Always asked same simple question: 'Anyone you know need inspection?'
- Thanked Mr. Patel after every referral, even if no sign-up

Total time invested over 3 years: About 2 hours of phone calls.

Total commission from that 2 hours: 62,000 dollars.

Nicole's philosophy: 'Past customers are sitting on a goldmine of future referrals. Most reps never go back to the well. I drink from it for years.'
successStories.keyTakeaway: Long-term customer relationships generate compounding referrals. A 5-minute call twice a year can generate thousands in commission.

sections.title: Building the Post-Installation Relationship
sections.content:
**From Transaction to Relationship**

Your work does not end when the installation is complete. The post-install period is when you transform customers into advocates who generate ongoing referrals for years to come.

**Why Post-Install Matters:**

**1. Referrals Are Your Best Leads**
- Pre-qualified and pre-sold by trusted source
- Higher conversion rates than cold knocking
- No objection handling required
- Faster sales cycle
- Better average ticket (trust is already established)

**2. Reviews Build Credibility**
- Online reviews overcome objections before you knock
- 5-star ratings differentiate you from competitors
- Reviews are permanent marketing assets
- New prospects research you before agreeing to inspection

**3. Yard Signs Generate Hyperlocal Leads**
- Neighbors see the sign and take action
- Pre-qualifies leads (same neighborhood, similar homes)
- Creates social proof ('my neighbor used them')
- Free, ongoing advertising in target areas

**4. Customer Advocates Sell For You**
- Word-of-mouth marketing is the most powerful
- Customers tell their story authentically
- Removes skepticism from prospects
- Creates a referral flywheel effect

---

**The Post-Install Follow-Up System:**

**IMMEDIATELY AFTER INSTALLATION (Same Day):**

**Your Action:**
- Thank the homeowner personally (call or in-person)
- Confirm satisfaction with completed work
- Set expectations for Certificate of Completion
- Explain final payment timeline

**Script:**
'Hi [Name]! I wanted to reach out and make sure you are happy with how everything turned out. [Listen to response] That is great to hear! The next step is the Quality Check meeting where you will sign the Certificate of Completion. After that is submitted to insurance, they will release the depreciation and you will make the final payment. In the meantime, if you have any questions or concerns, I am here to help.'

---

**WEEK 1-2 AFTER INSTALLATION:**

**Your Action:**
- Yard sign placement request
- Review request
- Initial referral conversation

**Yard Sign Script:**
'Hi [Name]! Now that your beautiful new roof is complete, I have a favor to ask. Would you be willing to let us place a yard sign in your front yard for a few weeks? It really helps us let your neighbors know we are working in the area. We will remove it whenever you want - just let us know.'

**Review Request Script:**
'I also wanted to ask if you would be willing to leave us a review online. Your feedback helps other homeowners make confident decisions, and it takes just a few minutes. I can send you a direct link that makes it super easy. Would that be okay?'

**Initial Referral Script:**
'One last thing - if you know any friends, family, or neighbors who might have storm damage, we would love to help them the same way we helped you. Do you know anyone who might benefit from a free inspection?'

---

**MONTH 1-3 AFTER INSTALLATION:**

**Your Action:**
- Check-in on satisfaction
- Request additional referrals
- Address any concerns immediately

**Check-In Script:**
'Hi [Name], I am just checking in to make sure everything is still looking great with your new roof and that you are happy with the work. [Listen] That is wonderful to hear! By the way, have any of your neighbors mentioned anything about getting their roof checked? We are still working in the area and would love to help them out too.'

---

**ONGOING (Quarterly or Semi-Annual):**

**Your Action:**
- Seasonal check-ins (spring, fall)
- Ask for referrals during peak storm seasons
- Maintain relationship for long-term referrals

**Seasonal Script:**
'Hi [Name], it is [Your Name] from Roof-ER. I hope you are doing well! We are heading into storm season, and I wanted to check in and see if you know anyone who might need their roof inspected. We are working in your area again and wanted to make sure your neighbors get taken care of like you did. Anyone come to mind?'

---

**Key Principles:**
- Make contact personal, not transactional
- Show genuine care for their satisfaction
- Ask for specific actions (yard sign, review, referral names)
- Make it easy for them (send direct links, handle logistics)
- Follow up multiple times (persistence without pestering)
- Express gratitude for every referral, regardless of outcome

sections.title: Strategic Referral Generation Systems
sections.content:
**Turning Customers Into Your Sales Team**

Referrals are the highest-quality leads you will ever receive. Master the art of generating them systematically.

**The Psychology of Referrals:**

**Why People Give Referrals:**
1. **Reciprocity** - You helped them, they want to help you
2. **Social status** - Sharing a great resource makes them look good
3. **Genuine care** - They want friends/family to benefit like they did
4. **Trust transfer** - Their trust in you extends to people they care about

**Why People Don't Give Referrals:**
1. **Never asked** - Most common reason
2. **Do not know how** - Unclear what to do
3. **Timing is wrong** - Asked when they are not thinking about it
4. **Fear of negative outcome** - Worried friend will have bad experience

**Your Solution:**
- ASK directly and specifically
- MAKE IT EASY with clear instructions
- ASK MULTIPLE TIMES at different stages
- PROVE YOUR VALUE through exceptional service

---

**The 4-Stage Referral Request System:**

**STAGE 1: At Full Approval (Week 2-3)**

**Context:** Homeowner just received full approval and is excited

**Script:**
'Congratulations on the approval! I am so glad we could help you get this taken care of. By the way, do you have any neighbors who might have storm damage too? I am already in the area and would love to help them the same way I helped you. Anyone come to mind?'

**Why It Works:**
- Homeowner is in peak positive emotion
- They are thinking about neighbors with similar homes
- You are already in the area (easy for you and them)

---

**STAGE 2: Right After Installation (Week 7-10)**

**Context:** Installation just completed, work looks beautiful

**Script:**
'Your new roof looks amazing! I bet your neighbors are going to be asking about it. When they do, I would love for you to share my information with them. I will make sure they get the same great experience you did. Sound good?'

**Why It Works:**
- The visible result creates natural conversation starters
- Neighbors will genuinely ask about the work
- You are priming them to share your info proactively

---

**STAGE 3: At Quality Check / Wrap Up (Week 9-12)**

**Context:** Final meeting, signing Certificate of Completion

**Script:**
'I just want to say thank you for trusting us with your home. If you know anyone - friends, family, neighbors, coworkers - who might need their roof inspected, I would be honored if you would share my information with them. Who comes to mind?'

**Why It Works:**
- Final positive interaction
- Gratitude triggers reciprocity
- Asking 'who comes to mind' prompts active thinking

---

**STAGE 4: Ongoing Check-Ins (Quarterly)**

**Context:** Seasonal follow-up calls

**Script:**
'Hi [Name]! It is [Your Name] from Roof-ER. Storm season is here, and I wanted to check if you know anyone who might need their roof inspected. We helped you [time period] ago, and I would love to take care of your neighbors the same way. Anyone you can think of?'

**Why It Works:**
- Regular reminders keep you top-of-mind
- Different seasons trigger different recall
- Persistence increases likelihood of capture

---

**Making Referrals Easy:**

**1. Direct Contact Exchange**
'Can I get their name and phone number? I will reach out directly and mention you sent me.'

**2. Give Them Your Card**
'Here are a few of my cards. Feel free to give them to anyone who asks about your roof.'

**3. Digital Sharing**
'I will text you my contact info. Feel free to forward it to anyone who needs a roof inspection.'

**4. Social Media Tagging**
'If you post about your new roof on social media, feel free to tag Roof-ER. We will share your post!'

---

**Tracking and Following Up on Referrals:**

**When You Receive a Referral:**
1. Thank the referrer immediately
2. Ask for context ('How do you know them? What should I mention?')
3. Contact the referral within 24 hours
4. Mention the referrer by name ('John Smith suggested I reach out')
5. Update the referrer on outcome (even if no sale)

**Referral Contact Script:**
'Hi [Referral Name], this is [Your Name] from Roof-ER. Your neighbor [Referrer Name] mentioned you might be interested in getting your roof inspected for storm damage. We just helped [him/her] get fully approved by insurance for a new roof, and [he/she] thought you might benefit from the same inspection. Do you have a few minutes to talk?'

---

**Referral Thank-You System:**

**For Referral That Leads to Inspection:**
- Text or call referrer: 'Thank you for the introduction to [Name]. I was able to inspect their roof today!'

**For Referral That Leads to Sign-Up:**
- Call referrer personally: 'I wanted to thank you for referring [Name]. We found qualifying damage and filed the claim today. I really appreciate you thinking of us!'
- Consider small thank-you gift (optional, check company policy)

**For Referral That Does Not Convert:**
- Still thank referrer: 'Thank you for introducing me to [Name]. Unfortunately they did not have qualifying damage, but I appreciate you thinking of us!'

**Key Principle:**
ALWAYS thank referrers regardless of outcome. This encourages future referrals.

sections.title: Yard Signs and Online Reviews - Your Passive Marketing
sections.content:
**Building Credibility While You Sleep**

Yard signs and online reviews work for you 24/7, generating leads and overcoming objections before you ever knock a door.

**YARD SIGNS: The Neighborhood Billboard**

**Why Yard Signs Matter:**
- **Hyperlocal targeting** - Neighbors see the sign in context
- **Social proof** - 'My neighbor trusted them'
- **Timing** - Sign is visible during peak storm damage awareness
- **Free advertising** - No ongoing cost, permanent visibility
- **Generates inbound leads** - Neighbors call you instead of you knocking

**The Yard Sign Request Script:**

**Timing:** 1-2 weeks after installation

**Script:**
'Hi [Name]! Your new roof looks fantastic. I wanted to ask a favor - would you be willing to let us put a yard sign in your front yard for a few weeks? It helps us let your neighbors know we are working in the area, and they often reach out when they see it.

We will place it respectfully, and you can have us remove it anytime - just let us know. Would that be okay?'

**Handling Hesitation:**

**'I do not want signs in my yard':**
'I totally understand! No problem at all. Would you be comfortable with us mentioning to your neighbors that we worked on your home if they ask?'

**'How long will it be there?':**
'Usually 2-4 weeks, but we will remove it anytime you want. Just give us a call or text and we will pick it up the same day.'

**'Will it damage my lawn?':**
'Not at all - the sign has small stakes that leave minimal marks, and your grass will recover within a few days of removal.'

**Yard Sign Best Practices:**
- Get explicit permission before placing
- Place in high-visibility location (near street)
- Ensure sign is clean, professional, and upright
- Remove promptly when requested
- Thank homeowner for allowing placement
- Track leads generated by each sign

---

**ONLINE REVIEWS: Your Digital Reputation**

**Why Reviews Matter:**
- **First impression** - Prospects research you before agreeing to inspection
- **Objection prevention** - Good reviews eliminate skepticism
- **Competitive advantage** - Differentiates you from other roofers
- **Permanent asset** - Reviews continue to work for you indefinitely
- **GAF Master Elite proof** - Supports your top 2% claim

**The Review Request Script:**

**Timing:** 1-2 weeks after installation (same time as yard sign)

**Script:**
'Hi [Name]! I am so glad you are happy with your new roof. I have a favor to ask - would you be willing to leave us a review online? Your feedback helps other homeowners feel confident in choosing Roof-ER, and it only takes a few minutes.

I can text you a direct link that makes it super easy - you just click, write a few sentences about your experience, and submit. Would that be okay?'

**Making It Easy:**
- Send direct review link via text or email
- Specify platform (Google, Yelp, Facebook)
- Provide simple instructions
- Follow up if they agree but do not complete (gentle reminder)

**Review Request Text Message Template:**
'Hi [Name]! Thank you again for choosing Roof-ER. Here is the link to leave a review - it only takes 2 minutes: [LINK]. We really appreciate your feedback!'

**Handling Hesitation:**

**'I do not usually leave reviews':**
'I completely understand. Your experience really helps other homeowners make good decisions though. Even just a few sentences and a star rating would mean a lot.'

**'I will do it later':**
'No problem! I will send you the link via text so you have it whenever you are ready. Just click and it takes you right there.'

**'I had one small issue':**
'I really appreciate you mentioning that. Let me make sure that gets addressed first. [Resolve issue] Now that it is taken care of, would you be willing to leave a review about your overall experience?'

---

**What to Request in Reviews:**

Suggest they mention:
- **Specific results:** 'Roof-ER helped me get my roof fully approved by insurance'
- **Your professionalism:** 'The sales rep was knowledgeable and professional'
- **The process:** 'They handled everything from inspection to claim filing'
- **The outcome:** 'I got a brand new roof and only paid my deductible'
- **Recommendation:** 'I highly recommend them to anyone with storm damage'

**Example Ideal Review:**
'Roof-ER was amazing from start to finish. [Your Name] did a thorough inspection and found hail damage I did not even know was there. He walked me through the entire insurance process and was at the adjuster meeting to represent me. My claim was fully approved, and I got a beautiful new roof for just my deductible. The installation team was professional and cleaned up everything. I highly recommend Roof-ER to anyone who needs their roof inspected!'

---

**Following Up on Review Requests:**

**1 Week After Sending Link:**
If no review posted, send gentle reminder:
'Hi [Name]! Just checking if you had a chance to leave that review. No pressure - I know you are busy! Here is the link again if you need it: [LINK]'

**After Review is Posted:**
Thank them immediately:
'Thank you so much for leaving that review! It really means a lot and helps other homeowners make confident decisions. I appreciate you!'

---

**Using Reviews in Your Pitch:**

Incorporate reviews into your Initial Pitch:
'We are GAF Master Elite certified - top 2% of roofing companies nationwide. You can look us up right now and see our 200+ five-star reviews. Homeowners consistently mention our professionalism and how we fight for full claim approvals.'

**Overcoming 'Too Many Roofers' Objection:**
'I totally get it! That is why I encourage you to look us up online right now. Check our reviews, see our credentials, and you will see we are not like the others. I will wait while you take a look.'

sections.title: Customer Service Excellence - Creating Advocates
sections.content:
**From Satisfied to Evangelical**

Good customer service creates satisfied customers. EXCELLENT customer service creates advocates who proactively sell for you.

**The Customer Experience Journey:**

**STAGE 1: Initial Contact (First Impression)**

**What Creates Positive Experience:**
- Professional appearance and communication
- Clear explanation of process
- Respectful of their time and property
- No pressure, just value
- Friendly, confident demeanor

**Your Actions:**
- Arrive on time (or communicate if delayed)
- Dress professionally (Roof-ER shirt, clean appearance)
- Maintain positive energy regardless of their mood
- Listen more than you talk
- Thank them for their time

---

**STAGE 2: Inspection & Documentation (Building Trust)**

**What Creates Positive Experience:**
- Thorough, professional inspection
- Clear communication about what you are doing
- Safety-conscious behavior
- Detailed explanation of findings
- Patient answering of questions

**Your Actions:**
- Explain what you will do before you do it
- Keep them informed during inspection
- Show them the photos and explain damage
- Use educational tone, not sales pressure
- Make complex insurance concepts simple

---

**STAGE 3: Claims Process (Managing Expectations)**

**What Creates Positive Experience:**
- Clear timeline expectations
- Regular updates on progress
- Proactive communication about delays
- Fighting for them when insurance pushes back
- Transparency about outcomes

**Your Actions:**
- Set realistic timelines upfront
- Provide weekly updates (at minimum)
- Notify them immediately of approvals or issues
- Escalate problems professionally
- Keep them CC-ed on all insurance communication

---

**STAGE 4: Installation (Delivering on Promise)**

**What Creates Positive Experience:**
- On-time installation
- Professional production team
- Clean worksite daily
- Addressing concerns immediately
- Quality workmanship

**Your Actions:**
- Confirm installation date in advance
- Check in during installation
- Address any homeowner concerns same-day
- Ensure thorough cleanup
- Be available for questions

---

**STAGE 5: Completion & Follow-Up (Creating Advocates)**

**What Creates Positive Experience:**
- Smooth final payment process
- Expressing gratitude for their business
- Staying in touch after completion
- Genuine care about their satisfaction
- Making them feel valued

**Your Actions:**
- Personal thank-you call or visit
- Request yard sign and review
- Check in 1 month after completion
- Seasonal follow-ups for referrals
- Immediate response to any post-install concerns

---

**Service Recovery: Handling Issues Professionally**

Problems will happen. How you handle them determines whether customers become advocates or detractors.

**The Service Recovery Framework:**

**1. Acknowledge Immediately**
'I hear you, and I understand why that is frustrating. Let me look into this right away.'

**2. Take Ownership**
'I am sorry this happened. I am going to personally make sure we get this resolved for you.'

**3. Investigate and Understand**
- Get all the facts
- Do not make assumptions
- Listen to their full concern

**4. Provide Solution**
'Here is what I am going to do to fix this: [specific actions]. I will follow up with you by [specific time] to confirm it is resolved.'

**5. Follow Through**
- Do exactly what you said you would do
- Follow up to confirm satisfaction
- Learn from the issue to prevent recurrence

**6. Go Beyond**
- Exceed their expectations in the resolution
- Show extra care and attention
- Turn the negative into a positive story they tell

**Key Principle:**
Customers who have issues that are resolved exceptionally well often become STRONGER advocates than customers who had no issues at all.

---

**Building Long-Term Relationships:**

**Annual or Semi-Annual Touch Points:**
- Send seasonal greetings (holiday cards, etc.)
- Provide home maintenance tips
- Remind them of warranty coverage
- Ask for referrals during peak storm seasons

**Remember Personal Details:**
- Note birthdays, anniversaries, life events in CRM
- Reference previous conversations
- Show you remember them as people, not transactions

**Be a Resource Beyond Roofing:**
- Recommend other contractors (HVAC, plumbing, etc.)
- Answer home maintenance questions
- Position yourself as a trusted home expert

**The Ultimate Goal:**
Create customers who proactively tell their story:

'You have to use Roof-ER. They helped me get a brand new roof through insurance, and I only paid my deductible. The whole process was smooth, and they fought for me when insurance tried to low-ball the claim. I cannot recommend them enough.'

**That testimonial is worth more than 100 cold-knocked doors.**

activities.title: Apply the 6-Step Service Recovery Framework
activities.description: Work through realistic service issues using the framework

scenarios.problem: Homeowner calls angry: 'Your production crew left trash in my yard and did not clean up properly!'
framework: 1. Acknowledge: 'You are absolutely right, that is unacceptable. I am so sorry that happened.'
2. Ownership: 'I am personally going to make sure this gets resolved today.'
3. Investigate: 'Can you tell me specifically what was left? I want to document everything.'
4. Solution: 'I am coming over in 2 hours with cleanup equipment to handle this myself.'
5. Follow Through: [Actually show up, clean thoroughly, document with photos]
6. Go Beyond: 'I also want to schedule our quality inspector to come verify everything is perfect. No charge.'
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Angry customer becomes impressed by responsiveness and personal accountability

scenarios.problem: Homeowner texts: 'I just noticed a shingle is loose on the ridge. This is frustrating.'
framework: 1. Acknowledge: 'Thank you for letting me know. I understand your frustration.'
2. Ownership: 'I am going to get our production supervisor on this immediately.'
3. Investigate: 'Can you send me a photo so I can see exactly what you are seeing?'
4. Solution: 'We will have a crew there tomorrow morning to inspect and repair. I will be there personally.'
5. Follow Through: [Crew fixes issue, you verify quality]
6. Go Beyond: 'I had the crew inspect the entire roof while they were there. Everything else is perfect. Here are photos.'
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Minor issue resolved so thoroughly that customer gains even more confidence

agnesContent.title: Agnes on Follow-Up Systems That Generate Referrals
agnesContent.content: Most reps make a critical mistake: they think their job ends at installation. Wrong. Installation is when the real work begins. Your satisfied customer is sitting on 10-20 potential referrals, but they will not magically appear. You have to activate them through systematic follow-up. Let me show you how.
points: Ask for referrals at FOUR stages: full approval, after install, quality check, and quarterly forever
The first referral request happens at full approval when they are most excited - do not wait
Set quarterly reminders for year one, semi-annual for year two, annual forever after
Make it EASY: get direct contact info, reach out yourself, mention the referrer by name
Thank referrers regardless of outcome - this encourages future referrals
agnesContent.realityCheck: One rep generated 47 sign-ups from a single satisfied customer over 6 months. Why? She asked for referrals at every stage and stayed in touch. That one relationship generated over 95,000 dollars in commission. How many satisfied customers are you leaving on the table?

agnesContent.title: Agnes on Asking for Referrals Without Being Pushy
agnesContent.content: Sales reps fear asking for referrals because they think it is pushy or awkward. Here is the truth: if you helped someone get a 30,000 dollar roof for just their deductible, asking them to share that value with others is NOT pushy - it is service. You are giving their friends the same opportunity. Reframe referral requests as helping, not asking.
points: Script: 'Do you know anyone who might benefit from a free inspection?' - Simple, direct, non-pushy
Timing is everything: Ask when they are happy (post-approval, post-install, post-quality check)
Make it collaborative: 'I would love to help your neighbors the same way I helped you'
Give them tools: Your business cards, digital contact info, easy ways to share
Follow up on every referral and report back - 'Thank you for the intro, we helped them!'
agnesContent.realityCheck: People WANT to help you if you helped them. The problem is not that they refuse - it is that you never ask. Ask at every stage. Make it easy. Follow through. Referrals become automatic.

agnesContent.title: Agnes on Yard Signs and Reviews - Marketing That Works While You Sleep
agnesContent.content: Yard signs and online reviews are passive marketing assets that generate leads 24/7. One yard sign can generate 5-10 inbound leads per month. One 5-star review overcomes objections for 50+ prospects. Yet many reps never request them. Do not make that mistake. Request yard signs and reviews within 1-2 weeks post-install, every single time.
points: Yard signs generate hyperlocal leads - neighbors see it and call YOU
Request yard sign placement 1-2 weeks post-install when work is visible and beautiful
Reviews overcome objections before you knock - prospects research you online first
Send direct review link via text - make it one-click easy
Follow up one week later if they have not posted: gentle reminder, no pressure
agnesContent.realityCheck: A yard sign costs the company 20 dollars. It generates 5-10 leads worth thousands in potential commission. Why would you NOT request placement on every job? Reviews are free marketing that works forever. Request them systematically.

agnesContent.title: Agnes on Building Relationships That Generate Lifetime Value
agnesContent.content: Think long-term. Nicole stayed in touch with the Patel family for 3 years. Total time invested: about 2 hours of phone calls. Total commission generated: 62,000 dollars. That is 31,000 dollars per hour. Why? Because she understood that past customers are sitting on future referrals. Set reminders. Make calls. Ask questions. Stay top-of-mind.
points: Year 1: Quarterly calls (4 touchpoints) - 'Storm season is here, anyone need inspection?'
Year 2: Semi-annual calls (2 touchpoints) - Reduce frequency but maintain connection
Year 3+: Annual calls (1 touchpoint) - Long-term referrals come from timing + trust
Remember personal details - birthdays, kids, life events - show you care about them as people
Be a resource beyond roofing - recommend contractors, answer home questions, build trust
agnesContent.realityCheck: Most reps never call a customer again after installation. That is leaving tens of thousands of dollars in referrals on the table. A 5-minute call twice a year can generate 10,000 dollars in commission. Do the math. Make the calls.

agnesContent.title: Agnes on Service Recovery - Turning Problems Into Advocacy
agnesContent.content: Brandon faced an angry customer. Nails in the driveway. Threat of bad review. He could have made excuses or blamed production. Instead, he arrived 2 hours later, spent 90 minutes picking up every nail, fixed a gutter issue he noticed, and followed up the next day. Result? 5-star review and 12 referrals. Problems are opportunities to demonstrate exceptional care.
points: Acknowledge immediately: 'You are right, that is unacceptable. I am sorry.'
Take ownership: 'I am personally going to fix this' - no blame, no excuses
Show up: Actions speak louder than words - be physically present to resolve
Go beyond: Fix the problem PLUS something extra they did not expect
Follow up: Verify satisfaction after resolution - close the loop
agnesContent.realityCheck: Customers who have problems resolved exceptionally well become STRONGER advocates than customers who never had problems. Service recovery is your moment to shine. Own it. Fix it. Exceed expectations. Turn detractors into evangelists.

quiz.question: When is the FIRST optimal time to ask for referrals?
options: During the initial inspection before finding damage
At full approval when homeowner is excited about claim approval (Week 2-3)
Only after installation is completely finished (Week 7-10)
Never ask - wait for them to offer referrals voluntarily
quiz.explanation: The FIRST optimal time to ask for referrals is at full approval (Week 2-3) when the homeowner is in peak positive emotion about getting their claim approved. They are excited, grateful, and thinking about neighbors with similar homes. This is before installation but after they have seen your value in getting approval. You will ask again at installation, quality check, and quarterly ongoing - but this first ask captures their peak enthusiasm.

quiz.question: When should you request yard sign placement?
options: During the initial pitch to pre-commit them
Right before the adjuster meeting for credibility
1-2 weeks after installation when work is visible and beautiful
At the project meeting before installation begins
quiz.explanation: Request yard sign placement 1-2 weeks after installation is complete. At this point, the work is visible and beautiful, creating natural conversation starters with neighbors. The homeowner can see the quality of the finished product and is proud to display the sign. This timing also ensures the roof is complete before advertising your work. Requesting earlier (before installation) is premature; requesting later misses the window of peak neighborhood visibility.

quiz.question: Why are online reviews critical for your sales success?
options: They increase your commission percentage automatically
They are required by GAF Master Elite certification annually
They overcome objections before you knock and differentiate you from competitors - prospects research you online first
They are only useful if you have over 500 reviews posted
quiz.explanation: Online reviews are critical because they work as permanent marketing assets that overcome objections BEFORE you ever knock on a door. Prospects research companies online before agreeing to inspections. When they see 200+ five-star reviews mentioning your professionalism and results, skepticism disappears. Reviews differentiate you from competitors and provide social proof of your expertise. They are not required for certification, they do not change commission, and even 20-30 quality reviews provide massive value.

quiz.question: What is the key principle of effective service recovery?
options: Avoid acknowledging problems to prevent customer complaints from escalating
Blame the production team to deflect personal responsibility
Customers who have problems resolved exceptionally well become STRONGER advocates than those who never had problems
Offer immediate discounts or refunds to make up for any service failures
quiz.explanation: The key principle is that customers who experience problems that are resolved EXCEPTIONALLY well often become STRONGER advocates than customers who never had issues at all. Why? Because exceptional service recovery demonstrates your character, responsiveness, and commitment. When you acknowledge immediately, take ownership, show up personally, go beyond fixing just the problem, and follow up - you create a story the customer tells enthusiastically. Brandon's nail cleanup story generated 12 referrals because Mrs. Johnson was so impressed by his response. Problems are opportunities to demonstrate excellence.

quiz.question: When should you thank a customer who gives you a referral?
options: Only if the referral results in a sign-up and commission
Only if the referral results in at least an inspection
ALWAYS - regardless of outcome - to encourage future referrals
Only after the referral's job is fully installed and paid
quiz.explanation: You should ALWAYS thank the referrer regardless of outcome. If the referral leads to an inspection, thank them. If it leads to a sign-up, thank them enthusiastically. If the referral had no damage or did not convert, STILL thank them. Why? Because thanking them reinforces the behavior and encourages future referrals. If you only thank them when it results in commission, they will hesitate to give referrals in the future (worried it might not work out and you will be disappointed). Gratitude regardless of outcome creates a referral culture.

quiz.question: How often should you follow up with customers in Year 1 post-installation for referrals?
options: Once immediately after installation, then never again
Monthly (12 times) to stay top-of-mind constantly
Quarterly (4 times) - seasonal check-ins during peak storm periods
Only when you happen to be working in their neighborhood
quiz.explanation: In Year 1, follow up QUARTERLY (4 times) - typically aligned with seasonal storm periods (spring, summer, fall, winter). This frequency keeps you top-of-mind without becoming annoying. Each quarterly call asks the same simple question: 'Storm season is here - anyone you know need their roof inspected?' In Year 2, reduce to semi-annual (2 times). Year 3+, annual (1 time). This systematic approach generated 31 referrals over 3 years for Nicole with the Patel family. Monthly would be too frequent; once and done leaves massive value on table.

quiz.question: What is the BEST way to make giving referrals easy for customers?
options: Tell them to have their friends call you when they are ready
Ask them to post about you on social media and hope friends see it
Get direct contact info (name and phone number) and reach out yourself, mentioning the referrer by name
Give them a stack of flyers to hand out to anyone interested
quiz.explanation: The BEST way is to get direct contact information (name and phone number) and reach out to the referral yourself, mentioning the referrer by name. This removes all burden from the customer. They just give you a name and number - you handle everything else. When you contact the referral, you say: 'Hi, your neighbor John Smith mentioned you might be interested in a free roof inspection.' This is far more effective than hoping the customer will have friends call you, post on social media, or distribute flyers. Make it one step for them: give you the name. You do the rest.

quiz.question: What should you do if a customer agrees to leave a review but has not done so after 1 week?
options: Assume they are not going to do it and move on
Send a gentle reminder with the review link again - no pressure
Call them and express disappointment that they have not followed through
Remove them from future referral requests as punishment
quiz.explanation: Send a gentle reminder after 1 week with the review link again, using friendly, no-pressure language. Most people genuinely intend to leave reviews but get busy and forget. A simple reminder like 'Hi! Just checking if you had a chance to leave that review. No pressure - I know you are busy! Here is the link again if you need it' is friendly, helpful, and often results in the review being posted. Never express disappointment, pressure them, or treat it as a failure on their part. Stay positive and make it easy.

quiz.question: Customer says: 'I do not want signs in my yard.' Best response?
options: 'That is fine, but you are missing out on helping your neighbors discover us.'
'No problem at all! Would you be comfortable with us mentioning to neighbors that we worked on your home if they ask?'
'I understand, but the sign will only be there 2 weeks - can we try it?'
'Okay, but we really need yard signs to grow our business.'
quiz.explanation: The best response is: 'No problem at all! Would you be comfortable with us mentioning to neighbors that we worked on your home if they ask?' This respects their boundary immediately (no pushback, no guilt), but offers an alternative that still provides value (permission to mention their home when neighbors inquire). Some homeowners do not want signs but are fine with word-of-mouth. This keeps the relationship positive while still seeking ways to generate neighbor leads. Pressuring them to reconsider or expressing disappointment damages the relationship.

quiz.question: Nicole generated 31 referrals from the Patel family over 3 years. What was her key strategy?
options: She visited their home in person every month to ask for referrals
She sent them expensive gifts to stay top-of-mind
She made quarterly calls Year 1, semi-annual Year 2, and annual Year 3+ asking simple question: Anyone need inspection?
She only reached out when she was working in their neighborhood
quiz.explanation: Nicole's strategy was systematic follow-up: Quarterly calls in Year 1 (4 touchpoints), semi-annual in Year 2 (2 touchpoints), and annual in Year 3+ (1 touchpoint). Each call asked the same simple question: 'Anyone you know need their roof inspected?' Total time invested over 3 years: about 2 hours of phone calls. Total commission generated: 62,000 dollars. The key was CONSISTENCY and SIMPLICITY. She did not need expensive gifts or in-person visits. Just regular, friendly check-ins asking a simple question. This generated compounding referrals as timing aligned with friends experiencing their own storm damage.

quiz.question: What is the correct order of the 6-Step Service Recovery Framework?
options: Investigate, Acknowledge, Solution, Ownership, Follow Through, Go Beyond
Acknowledge, Ownership, Investigate, Solution, Follow Through, Go Beyond
Ownership, Investigate, Acknowledge, Follow Through, Solution, Go Beyond
Acknowledge, Investigate, Ownership, Solution, Go Beyond, Follow Through
quiz.explanation: The correct order is: 1) Acknowledge immediately ('You are right, that is unacceptable'), 2) Take Ownership ('I am personally going to fix this'), 3) Investigate and Understand (get all facts), 4) Provide Solution (specific actions and timeline), 5) Follow Through (do exactly what you said), 6) Go Beyond (exceed expectations). This order matters: you must acknowledge and own the problem BEFORE investigating (shows you care more about them than defending yourself), provide a clear solution BEFORE taking action, and follow through BEFORE going beyond (do not over-promise and under-deliver).

quiz.question: Why do satisfied customers give referrals? (Select the PRIMARY psychological reason)
options: They feel obligated because you asked them to
Reciprocity - you helped them, they want to help you
They receive a financial incentive for each referral
They are trying to impress you with their social connections
quiz.explanation: The PRIMARY psychological driver is RECIPROCITY. You helped them get a 30,000 dollar roof for just their deductible. You saved them money, fought for their claim, and delivered quality work. Humans are wired to reciprocate value received. They WANT to help you because you helped them. This is why asking for referrals is not pushy - it is giving them an opportunity to reciprocate. The other drivers (social status, genuine care for friends) also matter, but reciprocity is the foundation. No financial incentive is needed - the value you provided IS the incentive.
